title: Acetone precipitation of proteins
author: Igem Dusseldorf
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8gehtte

steps.title: Add cold acetone and vortex
steps.instruction: Add acetone that has been pre‑chilled to –20 °C at a volume four times that of the protein extract, then vortex the mixture thoroughly.

steps.title: Incubate at -20 °C
steps.instruction: Place the tube at –20 °C and incubate for 2 hours.

steps.title: Centrifuge and discard supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the sample at 14 000 × g for 4 minutes at 4 °C, then carefully discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Wash pellet twice with acetone/water
steps.instruction: Perform two washes of the pellet using a 4:1 acetone‑to‑water mixture kept at –20 °C, centrifuging between washes.

substeps.instruction: Add enough 4:1 acetone/water mixture (pre‑chilled to –20 °C) to the pellet and vortex until the pellet is well broken up.
Repeat the addition of fresh 4:1 acetone/water mixture, vortex, and centrifuge under the same conditions for the second wash.

steps.title: Incubate to evaporate solvent
steps.instruction: After the final centrifugation, incubate the remaining solution at 40 °C until approximately 80 % of the liquid has evaporated.

steps.title: Resuspend and store pellet
steps.instruction: Resuspend the dried pellet in the remaining liquid. Store the suspension at –80 °C for long‑term use or at –20 °C for short‑term use.
